26:207.text: All that with which they used to enjoy shall not avail them.

26:208.text: And never did We destroy a township but it had its warners

26:209.text: By way of reminder, and We have never been unjust.

26:210.text: And it is not the Shayâtîn

26:211.text: Neither would it suit them, nor they can

26:212.text: Verily, they have been removed far from hearing it.

26:213.text: So invoke not with Allâh another ilâh
lest you should be among those who receive punishment.

26:215.text: And be kind and humble to the believers who follow you.

26:216.text: Then if they disobey you, say: "I am innocent of what you do."

26:217.text: And put your trust in the All-Mighty, the Most Merciful,

26:219.text: And your movements among those who fall prostrate
(to Allâh in the five compulsory congregational prayers)

26:220.text: Verily He, only He, is the All-Hearer, the All-Knower.

26:222.text: They descend on every lying, sinful person.

26:223.text: (to the devils and they pour what they may have heard of the Unseen from the angels)
, and most of them are liars.

26:224.text: As for the poets, the erring ones follow them,

26:225.text: See you not that they speak about every subject

26:226.text: And that they say what they do not do.

26:227.text: (in the Oneness of Allâh - Islâmic Monotheism)
and do righteous deeds, and remember Allâh much, and vindicate themselves after they have been wronged
[by replying back in poetry to the unjust poetry (which the pagan poets utter against the Muslims)]
. And those who do wrong will come to know by what overturning they will be overturned.
